name: Bone broth
description: Bones simmered for hours until the stock turns to jelly when cold.

tcm.note: Long-simmered bone soups are the archetypal warming tonic — gu tang builds qi, blood and marrow.

ayurveda.note: Mamsa rasa is ushna and building — given in convalescence.

unani.note: Yakhni is garam-tar, the standard Unani food for weakness and recovery.

histamine.note: The hours of simmering that make it nourishing are exactly what builds histamine — the reason a 'healing' broth flares some people badly.

guna.note: Aged, cured or fermented — the condition the texts call tamasic, whatever the ingredient started as.

effects.note: Small trials found that 3g of glycine before bed shortened time to fall asleep and improved sleep efficiency, one of them confirmed by lab sleep monitoring — but a cup of bone broth usually supplies less than that, commonly well under half to two-thirds of the trial dose, since home-simmered broth is far more diluted than a measured supplement. Only a long-simmered, bone-and-skin-heavy batch that sets to a firm jelly gets close to the amount tested. The evidence base is thin either way, a few dozen people across a handful of studies. A possible effect, not a promise — response to it varies from person to person.
